question: Where did the CNY balance come from?
known_information: Official rules select the route by source: documented current-account income, property sale, inheritance, emigrant property, prior FX, dividend, service payment or gift/no documents.
missing_information: The source of this specific balance.
answer_needed: Which lawful route, if any, fits this account?
how_to_discover: Collect bank statements and the document behind each large deposit; ask the bank in writing which route it will accept.

question: Which FX category did the bank assign to this account?
known_information: Decree 532 Art. 52(2) and PBOC Decree [2006] No. 3 Art. 28 define 境内个人/境外个人 differently.
missing_information: The account-holding bank's classification.
answer_needed: Do the domestic-individual convenience rules apply, or the foreign-individual documented-income rules?
how_to_discover: Request written confirmation of the account's 境内个人/境外个人 classification and the ID used at opening.

question: What are the 'considerable taxes' referred to in the brief?
known_information: No tax, rate, amount or office is named. No official page read imposes a tax on converting one's own CNY; PRC IIT attaches to underlying income/gain.
missing_information: The tax being quoted, its rate and assessing office.
answer_needed: Is there any PRC tax due before conversion, and on what income?
how_to_discover: Ask the bank/tax office for a written statement naming the tax and legal basis; obtain 完税凭证.

question: When and at what CNY/USD rate was the balance acquired?
known_information: 26 U.S.C. §988 treats disposition of nonfunctional currency as ordinary gain/loss; IRS yearly averages are labelled scenarios and 'IRS has no official exchange rate'.
missing_information: Acquisition dates and USD basis.
answer_needed: Is there a taxable U.S. currency gain, and how much?
how_to_discover: Reconstruct dated deposits and conversions; ask a U.S. tax professional to apply §988 and §988(e).

question: Is any part of the balance already foreign currency?
known_information: A foreign-currency account can be wired out; no conversion means no bid/ask spread.
missing_information: Currency composition of the account.
answer_needed: Can the cheapest wire-only route be used for part of the balance?
how_to_discover: Obtain a currency-by-currency account statement from the bank.

question: Is there an original exchange slip less than 24 months old?
known_information: Art. 60 permits reconverting unused RMB with the original slip within 24 months; small ID-only amounts are ≤USD 500/day (≤USD 1,000/day airside).
missing_information: Whether this account has such a slip and unused amount.
answer_needed: Can B04 or B05 be used?
how_to_discover: Locate the original 兑换水单 and compare its date/unused amount with the bank statement.

question: Is the money a gift, bequest or undocumented funds?
known_information: No official route for a foreign passport holder to convert undocumented/gift RMB was found; U.S. Form 3520 reports foreign gifts/bequests >USD 100,000.
missing_information: Donor, gift documents and bank's willingness.
answer_needed: Is there any lawful PRC conversion route at all?
how_to_discover: Ask the bank in writing; ask the donor about their own lawful remittance route; obtain U.S. Form 3520 advice.

question: Does conversion itself create a PRC tax?
known_information: No official page read imposes a tax on the act of conversion or wire; Decree 532 Art. 5 does not restrict genuine current-account transfers. The bank requires evidence that tax on underlying income was handled.
missing_information: None identified from the official pages read.
answer_needed: Treat spread and bank fees as conversion cost, not a conversion tax.
how_to_discover: Not needed for this question; see Q03 for any underlying tax.

question: What does the USD 50,000 annual convenience amount actually do?
known_information: It is a documentation threshold, not a hard cap; for FX purchase by an 境外个人, only PRC Foreign Permanent Resident ID holders get it on ID alone.
missing_information: None identified from the official pages read.
answer_needed: Do not assume a U.S. passport alone gives the purchase quota; documented transactions can exceed it.
how_to_discover: Not needed; see Q02 for the bank's classification.

question: Is tax record-filing required before the wire?
known_information: STA/SAFE 2013 No. 40 requires tax filing for single outbound payments above USD 50,000 for salary, dividends, real-estate transfer income etc.; the property guide waives the form at ≤USD 50,000.
missing_information: The payment category and whether the recordal already exists.
answer_needed: Which tax form must be presented to the bank?
how_to_discover: Ask the bank and local tax office for the exact 税务备案表 or 完税/免税证明 required for this payment.

question: Does a property-sale, inheritance or emigrant route apply?
known_information: Separate SAFE/PBOC routes exist for property sale, 继承转移 and 移民转移, each with approval/document list and tax certificate.
missing_information: Whether the facts fit any of those routes.
answer_needed: Which approval office and document set governs?
how_to_discover: Gather title/inheritance/hukou documents; ask the relevant SAFE office for a written eligibility decision.

question: Which routes are prohibited?
known_information: Quota splitting, private/app/underground swaps, crypto/stablecoin/RWA conversion, false documents and excess undeclared cash are prohibited by the cited PRC instruments.
missing_information: None identified from the official pages read.
answer_needed: Exclude those routes from the decision.
how_to_discover: Not needed; use qualified banks/licensed institutions only.

question: What is the executable rate and tariff for this branch?
known_information: BOC published the 2026/11/11 10:40:02 board (666.31/669.12 per 100 USD) and 1‰ wire fee (RMB 50-260) + RMB 150 cable; local/agreed/promotional differences are allowed.
missing_information: A dated written quote from the executing branch.
answer_needed: What CNY amount and itemised fees will actually be charged?
how_to_discover: Request a written pre-trade quote with rate timestamp, wire fee, cable, OUR option and receiving-bank charges.

question: What are OUR, intermediary and U.S. receiving fees?
known_information: BOC's 2014 personal notice gives historical USD 15/25 OUR surcharges; BOC's service page says intermediaries may deduct fees from principal. No current all-in figure is official.
missing_information: Current charge option and U.S. bank schedule.
answer_needed: How much will the U.S. account actually receive?
how_to_discover: Get the sending bank's charge-option confirmation and the U.S. bank's incoming-wire/international fee schedule.

question: Can the whole amount be sent in one wire?
known_information: Art. 65 states no amount threshold for an 境外个人's FX-account wire; Art. 64 requires documents above USD 50,000/day for 境内个人; approval routes may be remitted once or in instalments.
missing_information: Bank's approval and chosen route's wire schedule.
answer_needed: One wire or multiple wires/years?
how_to_discover: Ask the bank for a written remittance schedule after it reviews the documents.

question: Is cross-border RMB cheaper?
known_information: PBOC sources confirm a personal RMB salary remittance example and the 2018 policy, but publish no personal fee or offshore conversion rate.
missing_information: Sending and receiving bank quotes.
answer_needed: Can an all-in RMB→USD cost be computed?
how_to_discover: Request written RMB wire and offshore CNH conversion quotes for the exact amount.

question: Are ATM or cash routes practical?
known_information: ATM/card yearly cap RMB 100,000; cash export ≤USD 5,000 without permit, USD 5,000-10,000 with bank permit; U.S. declaration above USD 10,000.
missing_information: Itinerary, card fees, banknote fee, travel cost and time horizon.
answer_needed: Can these small-amount routes legally handle the balance?
how_to_discover: Ask the bank for its card/banknote tariff and compute the number of days/trips from the official caps.

question: Were prior FBARs filed?
known_information: FBAR is required if aggregate foreign accounts exceed USD 10,000 at any time; due Apr 15 with automatic extension to Oct 15.
missing_information: Prior-year FinCEN Form 114 confirmations.
answer_needed: Is a delinquent/streamlined procedure needed before or alongside the transfer?
how_to_discover: Retrieve BSA e-filing confirmations and IRS transcripts; consult a U.S. tax professional.

question: Were Forms 8938/3520 and worldwide income reported?
known_information: Form 8938 thresholds and penalties, Form 3520 foreign-gift threshold, and worldwide-income taxation are published by IRS.
missing_information: Copies of prior returns and information returns.
answer_needed: Which delinquent information-return procedure applies?
how_to_discover: Collect prior Forms 1040/8938/3520 and follow the IRS delinquent/streamlined pages with a professional.

question: Is any currency gain excluded as a personal transaction?
known_information: §988(e)(2) excludes personal-transaction gain up to USD 200; §988(e)(3) excludes §162/§212 expense transactions from personal treatment.
missing_information: Facts establishing the account's use and expense treatment.
answer_needed: Does §988 ordinary gain/loss apply?
how_to_discover: Have a U.S. tax professional document the account's use, acquisition basis and expense allocation.

question: Can PRC tax be credited in the U.S.?
known_information: The treaty Art. 22(2) allows a U.S. credit for Chinese income tax, and IRS explains the foreign tax credit/Form 1116, subject to limitations.
missing_information: None identified for the rule; the amount depends on Q03/Q04.
answer_needed: Claim the credit only for tax actually paid on the same income.
how_to_discover: Keep PRC tax certificates and have Form 1116 prepared with the U.S. return.

question: Which correction procedure fits past non-willful noncompliance?
known_information: SFOP (foreign residency) has no streamlined penalty; SDOP has a 5% miscellaneous offshore penalty; delinquent information-return and delinquent-FBAR procedures are also published.
missing_information: Residency, prior filings, willfulness and IRS contact status.
answer_needed: SFOP, SDOP, delinquent procedures or voluntary disclosure?
how_to_discover: Complete the IRS eligibility checks with a U.S. tax professional before filing.

question: Does the foreign earned income exclusion help?
known_information: FEIE applies to foreign earned income from personal services; pension, annuity and investment/currency gains are not foreign earned income.
missing_information: None identified for the rule.
answer_needed: Do not use FEIE to shelter existing savings or currency gain.
how_to_discover: Not needed for this question.

question: Which method has the lowest lawful all-in cost?
known_information: This edition computes only the published BOC bank benchmark. All-in totals require branch quote, intermediary/receiving fees, PRC tax and U.S. §988 treatment.
missing_information: Q01-Q23 answers.
answer_needed: A defensible, case-specific least-cost/lawful ranking.
how_to_discover: Complete the P0 questions first, then request written quotes for the two eligible routes and compare all-in USD received.

question: What is the U.S. receiving account and payee identity?
known_information: BOC's wire form requires currency/amount, payee name/address, account number, bank name and SWIFT code or address.
missing_information: Verified receiving-bank details.
answer_needed: Can the wire be addressed to the correct account without a return/reversal?
how_to_discover: Obtain the receiving bank's written wire instructions and confirm the payee name matches the PRC account holder.

question: What is the deadline and urgency?
known_information: Quota convenience amounts reset by calendar year; ATM/card cap is per calendar year; tax and reporting due dates are fixed by IRS/FinCEN.
missing_information: The user's deadline.
answer_needed: Can a multi-year quota/ATM route be considered, or is a documented single-wire route required?
how_to_discover: Write down the target date and compare it with the official calendar-year and filing deadlines.

question: Which records must be retained?
known_information: Bank wire form, rate confirmation, source/tax evidence, approval letters, FBAR/8938/3520 filings and Form 1116 support are all documented requirements or consequences in the cited pages.
missing_information: None identified for the record types.
answer_needed: Keep a complete audit trail before and after the transfer.
how_to_discover: Create a dated folder with bank, tax and U.S. filing documents; retain per each form's instructions.

question: Which inherited repo figures should be trusted?
known_information: Sibling layers use three different BOC board snapshots; some cite a dead PBOC Beijing URL and older flags. This edition uses its own dated snapshot and flags each discrepancy.
missing_information: A final integrator's chosen snapshot.
answer_needed: Which layer is the current source of truth?
how_to_discover: Compare the dated Sources pages; use the latest quoted board and live URLs, and keep older pages as historical.

question: Is a licensed non-bank payment institution available?
known_information: SAFE says personal FX must go through qualified banks, licensed exchange institutions or authorised agencies; no official page read confirms a named provider for this exact outbound personal balance or its price.
missing_information: Provider licence and written terms for mainland outbound transfers.
answer_needed: Is there a lawful non-bank channel at all?
how_to_discover: Ask the provider for its licence and written mainland-outbound personal RMB terms; verify the licence with the regulator.

question: Should the 10% treaty rate be used for a dividend?
known_information: Treaty Art. 9(2) caps source-state dividend tax at 10% for a beneficial owner; STA 2019 No. 35 requires self-assessment, report form and retained tax-residency/beneficial-owner documents.
missing_information: Whether this balance is a dividend and whether the evidence exists.
answer_needed: 20% statutory IIT or a valid 10% treaty position?
how_to_discover: Obtain the company resolution, tax-residency certificate and written withholding-agent treatment; consult a PRC/U.S. tax professional.
